name: queue_basic
kind: survey, supplement to v1: the three points v1 left open that decide how the queue and the SM store rate are written -- in which order entries of different kinds leave the per-warp queue when the kinds alternate, what makes a global store slow at the SM (width below a word, a different word, a different line) -- plus the SM rate of the other queue kinds and the control cell of the wide-slot LDS; installs nothing
mechanisms: per-warp queue of 10 (queue_basic v1): service across kinds
SM-level rate of global stores by address form; SM-level rate of LDS, LDG, SHFL.IDX and the wide shared stores
why: queue_basic v1 addendum (readings), last paragraph. The installation protocols of the queue and of the SM store rate need these before their rules are written.
data_seen_before_freezing: queue_basic v1 readings (its addendum): one queue of 10 per warp shared by STS, LDS, SHFL.IDX, LDG, STG; r = 2 (LDS), 4 (STS, SHFL.IDX, LDG), 6 (STG), 8 (STS.64, STG.64), 10 (STS.128), 12 (STG.128); in sequences of 10 a then 6 b, b waits at a's pace. SM rate: one STS per cycle, one 4-byte STG to the same word per 2.0 cycles; per STG per SM at 16 warps 1.94 / 1.95 (4 B, same word), 7.2 / 4.6 (2 B, same word), 7.7 / 4.2 (eight lines per warp), 10.0 / 4.9 (fresh lines). Reader behind stores: +3.0 per STS, about +5.3 per STG; the LDS of the wide slot sits 12-13 above the plain cells, with no cell without stores.

mem_basic v1 mixes (4 + 4, below the depth): four STG between four LDG delay the loads' reader by 20; four LDS or S2R between four LDG do not delay it; four STS between four LDS delay the LDS reader by 16.

probe.chain: As v1: frame q.loop.ptx unchanged, generator gen_queue.py extended by the forms below, conventions of v1 including its addendum of realisation notes (read barriers, barrier-0 wait, host check); case list tools/microbench/queue_basic/cases-v2.txt; run root $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/queue_basic-v2/<device>; replay build b046ee5c.

new producers.stgw4: STG.E desc[UR][Routw.64 + 4 (k mod 4)], Rtid: 4-byte store, producer k to word k mod 4 of the thread's 16-byte slot of the wide output block (the same 128-B line for a thread, four lines per warp).
new producers.stgw1: as stgw4 but always word 0 of the slot (control of the wide block's layout).
new producers.stg8: STG.E.U8 desc[UR][Rout.64], Rtid: 1-byte store to the thread's word of the narrow block.
new producers.stgd2: as v1's stgd with line k mod 2.
new producers.ldsx: v1's 4-byte LDS of the wide shared slot.

probe.cell forms: v1's run, rate and forward forms, and alternation q.alt.<a>_<b>.n<N>: producers a, b, a, b, ... (N in all) in consecutive slots, reader behind the last when it is a load.

cells.A alternation, one warp: q.alt.sts_lds.n24, q.alt.stg_ldg.n24, q.alt.sts_stg.n24, q.alt.lds_ldg.n24, q.alt.stg_lds.n24; q.alt.sts_stg.n16, q.alt.lds_ldg.n16.
cells.B store form at the SM (rate cells, 10 s: q.stgw4.e3.w16, q.stgw1.e3.w16, q.stg8.e3.w16, q.stgd2.e3.w16, q.stg64.e3.w16, q.stg128.e3.w16; one warp: q.stgw4.e3, q.stg8.e3.
cells.D wide-slot LDS: q.fwd.sts0_lds2.x (two LDS of the wide slot, no store), q.ldsx.n24.
cells.unrealised: as v1, recorded in tools/microbench/queue_basic/unrealised-v2.txt before the run.

derivation.alternation: sustained cycles per producer = loop total / N for the n24 cells (the queue does not drain between iterations) and the wait at issue per producer for the n16 cells; reader wait.
derivation.SM: cycles per producer per SM = loop total / (producers per iteration x 16); classes on the producers.

questions_before_data.Q1 (order across kinds): Candidates. (O-serial) one server: entries are served one after another whatever their kind; sustained cycles per producer = the mean of the two r: sts_lds 3.0, stg_ldg 5.0, sts_stg 5.0, lds_ldg 3.0, stg_lds 4.0. (O-two) one server for the shared-memory kinds and one for the global kinds, entries leave the queue in issue order: within a side as serial (sts_lds 3.0, stg_ldg 5.0), across sides the slower side sets the pace: sts_stg 3.0 (6 per pair), lds_ldg 2.0, stg_lds 3.0. Expected from mem_basic's mixes: (O-two). The n16 cells show the same on the waits behind producer 10.
questions_before_data.Q2 (what makes a store slow at the SM): Candidates. (W-same) only a store to the address of the store in front of it in the SM's store path is fast (merged); anything else pays the slow rate: stgw4 slow, stgd2 slow, stgw1 fast, stg8 open. (W-word) a store of a full word to a line already in the store path is fast, sub-word stores are slow: stgw4 fast, stgw1 fast, stg8 slow, stgd2 fast or between. (W-line) the number of lines a warp writes sets the rate: stgw1 and stgw4 alike (four lines per warp) between the one-line 1.95 and the eight-line 7.7 / 4.2, stgd2 between as well. STG.64 / .128 at the SM: open (v1: one line 2.0 at 4 B).
questions_before_data.Q3 (SM rate of the other kinds): Cycles per producer per SM at 16 warps for LDS, LDG, SHFL.IDX, STS.64, STS.128 against STS 0.98; mem_basic had LDG 1.04 (ldg.n16.w16, without read barriers and on the m2 frame).
questions_before_data.Q4 (wide-slot LDS): Is the 12-13 of v1's .x cells the LDS of the wide slot itself (q.fwd.sts0_lds2.x reader about 35 against 23.0 / 22.8) and what is its r in a run (q.ldsx.n24 against LDS 2.0)?

install: Nothing. Readings go into the addenda.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case or error used to choose a rule or a value; no cell dropped after its data is seen.

addenda.when: 2026-11-22, before the run (realisation of the probes; no data)
addenda.text: All 24 cells are realised on both targets (unrealised-v2.txt: none; realised forms stgw4 STG.E desc[UR8][R2.64+0x4 / +0x8 / +0xc], stgw1 STG.E desc[UR8][R2.64], stg8 STG.E.U8 desc[UR8][R12.64] from a new q_donor line, stgd2 STG.E desc[UR8][R12.64(+0x80)], ldsx LDS [R97]). q_loop is unchanged: its raw listing is byte-identical on both targets and the 148 plan files of v1 are byte-identical after regeneration; q.nop, q.nop.w16 and q.ldg.n16 are v1's probes. The offset of stgw4 is in bytes (word k mod 4 of the 16-byte slot). The one-warp and 16-warp cells of q.stgw4.e3 and q.stg8.e3 share a probe. Conventions as v1's realisation notes; the host check of stored values covers the new store forms (stgw4: the four words of the slot, stgw1: its first word, stgd2: the second line; stg8 needs nothing beyond the thread's word). Plan checks: the 19 new plans pass check_m_plans.py on both targets.

addenda.when: 2026-11-22, readings of the run (clone stall-attribution-52 at 4af1011f; jobs mechver-queue2-h100 on gpu-h100-0298 and mechver-queue2-b300 on gpu-b300-0824; roots $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/queue_basic-v2/{h100,b300}; replay build b046ee5c; tables in $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/queue_basic-v2-readings: <device>.{role,pc}.tsv, <device>.onset.txt, brief.txt)
addenda.text: Run: on both devices 24 of 24 cells pass the loop gate, the direct run, the check word and the stored-value check, are captured, have both reference passes (48 of 48 with rc 0) and are replayed; sync_basic_RC 0. Values per warp and iteration, H100 / B300, hardware pass a. A correction of the derivation first: 'loop total / N' is the sustained cycles per producer only in cells without a reader (q.alt.sts_stg); in the cells that end in a reader the reader's wait drains the queue every iteration, so those are read from the waits at issue behind the onset (wait + 1 per producer). Q1 (order across kinds): (O-serial) on both devices; the expectation (O-two) is wrong. Behind the onset (producer 11 or 12) each producer waits its own kind's r - 1 whatever the other kind is: q.alt.sts_lds.n24 STS 3.00 / 2.96 and LDS 0.98 / 1.02 (6.0 per pair); q.alt.stg_ldg.n24 STG 4.93 / 5.09 and LDG 2.97 / 2.95 (9.9 / 10.0 per pair); q.alt.sts_stg.n24 STS 3.02 / 3.08 and STG 4.93 / 5.00, loop total 120.8 / 121.0 = 5.03 / 5.04 per producer where (O-two) said 3.0; q.alt.lds_ldg.n24 LDS 1.03 / 1.02 and LDG 2.92 / 2.99 (6.0 per pair; (O-two) said 4); q.alt.stg_lds.n24 STG 4.91 / 4.94 and LDS 0.96 / 1.00 (7.9 per pair; (O-two) said 6); the n16 cells the same on producers 11-16 (sts_stg: 1.0, 5.0, 2.7, 4.8, 3.1, 5.0 / 1.1, 5.1, 2.8, 5.3, 2.9, 4.9; lds_ldg: 0.0, 0.9, 1.0, 2.8, 1.3, 2.9 / 0.0, 1.1, 1.0, 2.9, 0.8, 3.2). So the ten slots of a warp are released one after another, each entry holding the release for its own r, across shared and global kinds. Class of the wait in the mixed cells: mio_throttle on every producer of sts_stg, lds_ldg and stg_lds including the STG and LDG (v1's rule: lg_throttle only when waiter and the entries in front are all global; stg_ldg is lg_throttle throughout). Readers: 43.8 / 47.9 (pass b 43.9) behind sts_lds, 76.1 / 77.8 behind stg_ldg, 58.5 / 58.3 behind lds_ldg, 54.2 / 53.9 behind stg_lds; the replay has 22.0 / 21.0, 72.6 / 59.6, 57.7 / 45.7, 22.0 / 21.0. Not explained here: twelve LDS between twelve LDG leave the loads' reader at 58.5 / 58.3, no later than eight LDG alone (mem_basic 59.0 / 61.7), although each LDS holds the release for 2 cycles -- the time a load's result returns is not simply its slot's release plus a constant; the stores in front of an LDS do delay its reader (v1 Q6). Q2 (what makes a store slow at the SM, 16 warps, cycles per store per SM = loop total / 160): none of the three candidates as written. What decides is how many lines one store instruction of a warp writes and whether it is a whole-word store to the line the warp's previous store wrote: 4-byte store, one line per warp, same word (v1 q.stg.e3.w16) 1.94 / 1.95; 1-byte store to that word (q.stg8) 7.21 / 4.58, as v1's 2-byte store (7.18 / 4.60); 4-byte store alternating between two lines (q.stgd2) 4.84 / 3.32; and every form whose 32 lanes span four lines is five to ten times slower still: q.stgw1 (4 bytes, always the first word of the 16-byte slot) 44.3 / 20.0 (H100 pass b 46.8), q.stgw4 (the four words in turn) 46.7 / 20.0, q.stg64 43.2 / 20.1, q.stg128 36.6 / 18.2 (H100 pass b 34.1). stgw1 against stgw4 shows that writing a different word does not matter ((W-same) and (W-word) both fail on stgw1); (W-line) named the right variable and the wrong size (it expected the four-line forms between 1.95 and the eight-line cell's 7.7 / 4.2). Per line written the four-line forms cost 9-12 / 4.5-5.0, the range of v1's fresh-line and eight-line cells (10.0 / 4.9, 7.7 / 4.2). The replay's store_buffer charges by line at about 8.4 / 4.6: its loop totals are 5384 / 2964 against the hardware's 7473, 7088, 6904, 5850 / 3196, 3203, 3208, 2905 for the four-line forms (H100 8-28 % short, B300 within 8 %), 1354 / 742 against 1153 / 733 for the 1-byte store, and 1354 / 742 against 774 / 532 for the two-line alternation: the replay lacks the fast path (whole-word store to the previous store's line, fully at one line, partly at two) and is about right elsewhere. One warp: q.stgw4.e3 7.62 / 7.68 cycles per store with lg_throttle (the four-line 4-byte store sustains 7.6 in the per-warp queue where the one-line store has 6.0; the replay has 31 / 17), q.stg8.e3 as q.stg.e3 (5.97 / 6.01). Q3 (SM rate of the other kinds, 16 warps): LDS 0.99 / 0.98, LDG 0.98 / 0.99, SHFL.IDX 0.98 / 0.99 cycles per producer per SM -- the same one per cycle as STS; STS.64 3.98 / 3.97, STS.128 3.98 / 4.55. The wait sits on the producers (LDS mio_throttle 79.1 / 81.6 + not_selected 27.0 / 24.2; LDG lg_throttle 72.7 / 73.6 + 24.0 / 24.2; SHFL.IDX 78.3 / 79.8 + 26.7 / 26.9; STS.64 887.5 / 886.0 + 43.4 / 43.1; STS.128 887.5 / 1029.9 + 44.3 / 48.1) and the readers wait 62.5 / 62.0, 71.7 / 72.9, 62.9 / 62.2. The replay has the loop totals of LDS and LDG (253.5 / 254.6 against 252.5 / 251.3; 263.3 / 256.7 against 249.8 / 252.9) with all of the wait on the reader (153.6 / 155.1, 162.0 / 156.3), SHFL.IDX 18 % short (205.4 / 206.7 against 252.0 / 253.1) and the wide shared stores far short (343 / 150 and 646 / 150 against 1018 / 1016 and 1019 / 1165). Whether the one-per-cycle is one limit shared by the kinds is not measured (every cell has one kind). Q4 (wide-slot LDS): it is the load, not the stores -- q.fwd.sts0_lds2.x reader 34.8 / 34.5 against the plain cell's 23.0 / 22.8 (the 11.8 / 11.7 of v1's .x cells). In a run (q.ldsx.n24) it takes its queue slot like any LDS (waits from producer 14 at 1.0, r = 2.0) but its results return 6.2 apart: reader 178.1 / 177.5 against 34.2 / 34.2 for the narrow word; v1's LDS.128 of the same slot had 107.7 / 107.3 behind 12 (6.6 apart). The slot is 16 B per thread, so one LDS of a warp spans 512 B; the narrow word spans 128 B. The replay has 92.6 / 68.6 and 26.9 / 25.0. Left for the installation protocols: the result time of a load against its slot's release; the SM limit across kinds; the two-line store rate.
